review_agent_is_blocked_on_us: Its recent commits all say 'audit paused, queue full'. It stops auditing while open/ is large, so throughput is limited by the fix agent, not the reviewer. Draining open/ unblocks new findings.
operational_rules_learned_the_hard_way: backend `npm run lint` is `eslint --fix` and rewrites source. Gate on `npx eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` instead.
Run backend unit tests as `TZ=UTC npm run test:unit`; some specs count periods against fixtures and flip under other offsets.
Jest here is v30: the flag is `--testPathPatterns` (plural).
Frontend `npm run test` takes ~9 minutes (628 files). Iterate with `npx vitest run <path>`; run the full suite once before pushing.

A FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED in this sandbox. To wait for a long job, start it with run_in_background and then start a second background `until ! pgrep -f vitest; do sleep 10; done` job -- the harness notifies you when each exits. Chained short sleeps are blocked too.

NEVER git stash to check that a test fails without the fix while a full-suite run is in flight -- the running suite reads the reverted file mid-run and its result is worthless. Do the revert check on the single file FIRST, then start the full suite, then leave the tree alone.
transactions.status is NULLABLE (schema.sql:274). Never `status != 'VOID'` / `Not(TransactionStatus.VOID)`; use the entity's isVoid getter in JS or `(t.status IS NULL OR t.status != 'VOID')` in SQL.
Reuse an existing translated key across namespaces where the copy is identical. A new en-only errors.json key costs ~36 parity failures.

A nested withScopedDb JOINS the ambient transaction, so an assertXOwned helper opening its own withScopedDb still refuses before the caller's write. Findings written against pre-RLS code will ask for a QueryRunner manager -- there are none left in src/ and lint bans them.
createScopedDbMocks THROWS for an unregistered entity: adding a repository read means registering [Entity, mock] in the spec.
Verify every regression test by actually reverting the fix and re-running. Some tests deliberately pass either way; only the revert run tells those apart from vacuous ones.

A mock must have the shape the real collaborator returns. `{ data: [...] }` with no `pagination` makes fetchAllAccountTransactions throw on `result.pagination.hasMore` -- four mocks in LoanAmortizationReport.test.tsx were like that and passed only because the component swallowed the throw, with waitFor returning on its first success before the error landed. When you remove a swallow, expect to fix mocks that were leaning on it, and treat a test asserting 'handles X error gracefully' by checking the body still renders as the defect written down as an expectation.

vitest `import.meta.glob('/src/...', {query:'?raw', eager:true, import:'default'})` is how the guard tests read source. Pair every scanning assertion with a second one pinning the glob's match count, or a glob that matches nothing passes vacuously forever.
escalate_rather_than_implement: Most of what remains in open/ is financial calculation. Escalate (write a DEC, flip requires_human_approval, leave in open/) when the finding admits more than one defensible numeric answer -- the common case in loan-schedule.ts, loan-history.ts and rate-change-inference.service.ts. REV-004 (annualization by calendar-day gaps) changes the inference formula and is the clearest example. Implement only where an explicit CLAUDE.md rule or an in-repo pattern fixes the answer, as with REV-039 ('a failed lookup is not an empty dataset', plus an existing useReportData/ReportError pattern to copy).
